chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed while traveling and completed the prayer. He said: 'If it was within the time, let him repeat it; and if the time has passed, then no (he does not need to repeat).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a traveler prays four rakats instead of two?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the specific ruling for a traveler who erroneously performs the full four-rakat prayer (Tamam) instead of the shortened two-rakat prayer (Qasr). The Imam distinguishes between praying within the designated time, which necessitates repetition to fulfill the obligatory shortened form, and praying after the time has expired, where the prayer is considered valid and no repetition is required. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of the prayer depends on the timing of the act relative to the obligation's window.
